source_documents.title: Orthogonally Arranged π-Electronic Systems with Anion-Responsive Moiety Exhibiting Photoinduced Electron Transfer

reference_evidence_units.quote: Transient absorption measurements of the acridine-substituted dpp revealed a photoinduced electron transfer from the anion-responsive unit to the electron-deficient moiety, which was accelerated by anion binding.
reference_evidence_units.statement: PET from dpp to acridine, faster in the Cl- complex.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These results suggest that the transient absorption bands of 1 at 650 and 460 nm can be assigned to the radical anion of the acridine moiety and the radical cation of the dpp moiety, generated by intramolecular electron transfer from the dpp moiety to the acridine moiety.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Radical-ion bands identify the charge-separated state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The time constant for electron transfer was estimated to be 1.4 ps.
reference_evidence_units.statement: ET in 1.4 ps; the CT state lives for nanoseconds.

reference_evidence_units.quote: whereas the introduced acridine unit was nearly orthogonal to the core with a dihedral angle of 75.6°
reference_evidence_units.statement: Acceptor is nearly orthogonal to the donor.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Femtosecond TA shows acridine radical anion and dpp radical cation formed in 1.4 ps; the orthogonal donor-acceptor arrangement is the design.
